deep.reconstruction:
There is no mathematics on this page: no derivation, formula or computation. It is a planning list headed 'Noch zu lesende Vorlesungen' ('Lectures still to be given'), part of the numbered sequence of Hilbert's notebook pages (111, 112, 113). It almost certainly dates from his Königsberg years as Privatdozent and Extraordinarius (c. 1886-1894). The pattern of strike-throughs suggests he crossed out a course once he had delivered it.

Crossed out (presumably already given):
- ordinary differential equations
- calculus of variations
- analytic geometry
- theory of functions of a complex variable
- analytic mechanics
- elliptic functions
- theory of definite integrals by Cauchy's method (residue calculus)
- on the problem of the quadrature of the circle (transcendence of π)
- on the concept of number (irrational numbers, countability, complex numbers, quaternions)
- on Bernoulli numbers

Not crossed out (still planned):
- theory of functions of a real variable
- introduction to potential theory
- on higher algebraic surfaces
- theory of cyclotomy (Kreistheilung)
- reciprocity law for quadratic and higher power residues
- Abelian functions
- probability theory and the method of least squares
- overview of methods and theories in mathematics (concepts of divisibility and of magnitude)

The next page continues the list: axioms of geometry for hearers of all faculties, algebraic functions of one variable, and the PDEs of physics. It also has some dates, possibly 1891 and 1888. Nothing needs to be computed or filled in.

results.what: A list of planned and completed lecture courses, documenting the breadth of Hilbert's teaching programme. The planned items include cyclotomy and higher reciprocity laws, which anticipate his later Zahlbericht work, and the 'Zahlbegriff' course, which anticipates his foundational interests.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a purely administrative list of lecture topics with no mathematical content. It is well documented that Hilbert, as a Königsberg Privatdozent, deliberately lectured on a new subject almost every semester. These topics match his known teaching and research interests (number theory, invariants and algebraic geometry, function theory, foundations).
transcription_corrections: 'Ueberblick über Methoden' is written 'Ueberblick über d. Methoden' (with an abbreviated article 'd.') in the manuscript.
'Ueber Bernoullische[?] Zahlen' is confirmed as 'Ueber Bernoullische Zahlen' (struck through); the [?] can be removed.
'Warscheinlichkeitsrechnung' is indeed spelled without the 'h' in the manuscript; the transcription is faithful.
'Potenz-reste' is hyphenated across lines as 'Potenz=' / 'reste' (double hyphen) in the original.
